title: Bounded Friend Suggestions
real_world_story: When recommending new connections ('People You May Know'), a social network cannot explore the entire global graph of hundreds of millions of users without timing out. Instead, recommendation workers perform a bounded search constrained to a depth limit K (such as K = 2 for friends-of-friends). The engine must identify all candidate users reachable within at most K hops who are not already direct friends of the target user and not the target user themselves.
problem_statement: Given an unweighted network of N users and M bidirectional friendships, discover all candidate friend suggestions for a target user S within a maximum search depth of K hops. A candidate user C is eligible if the shortest path distance d between S and C satisfies 2 <= d <= K. Direct friends (distance 1) and user S itself (distance 0) are excluded. Return all eligible candidate IDs in ascending numerical order. If no eligible candidate exists, print NONE.
task: Find all users whose shortest path distance d from user S satisfies 2 <= d <= K, and print their IDs sorted in ascending order separated by a single space, or NONE.
input_format:
The first line contains three space-separated integers N, M, and K, denoting the number of users, friendships, and maximum depth limit.
The next M lines each contain two space-separated integers u and v, representing an undirected friendship.
The final line contains an integer S, the source user ID.
output_format: Print the space-separated list of candidate user IDs in ascending numerical order. If no candidates satisfy the condition, print NONE.

examples.explanation: From user 1: direct friends at distance 1 are {2, 3}. User 4 is at distance 2 (via 1->2->4 or 1->3->4), which is <= K=2. User 5 is at distance 3 (> K). Thus, user 4 is the only suggestion.
All other users (2, 3, 4) are direct friends at distance 1. No users exist at distance 2 <= d <= 2, so output NONE.

real_world_takeaway: Imposing strict depth boundaries on graph exploration prevents combinatorial explosion in high-degree social networks, ensuring real-time recommendation responses.
